subject: mathematics
question_text: Prove that the real valued function f(x) = x/(eˣ − 1) + x/2 + 1 is an even function on R − {0}.

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), book p.15, chapter 2 FUNCTIONS, Very Short Answer question 25. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. ⚠ THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The 1+1 shape gives one mark to replacing x by −x and clearing e⁻ˣ, and one to the algebra that turns the result back into f(x), because those are two separate pieces of work and a student who stops after the first has done half. The domain condition x ≠ 0, and the fact that R − {0} contains −x whenever it contains x, are carried in the written lines where the student reads them, not only in this note. Paper position: Maths-1A Section A runs Q1–Q10 at 2 marks each, all compulsory. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would prove this — what you write first, how you clear e to the minus x, and what you compare at the end.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write f(−x) and clear e⁻ˣ
steps.margin_note: One mark for replacing x by −x and clearing e⁻ˣ. Say first that −x is in the domain; a parity proof on a domain that is not symmetric is meaningless.
steps.memory_tip: Replace e⁻ˣ by 1/eˣ and multiply the top and the bottom by eˣ. That one move clears every negative power.
lines: so f(−x) is defined for every such x.

recall.must_convey: That f(−x) is written by replacing x with −x, and that e⁻ˣ − 1 = (1 − eˣ)/eˣ turns the first term into xeˣ/(eˣ − 1).
accept: put minus x in place of x everywhere

multiply the top and bottom by e to the x
the first term becomes x e to the x over e to the x minus one
e power minus x ni one by e power x ga rasi eˣ tho multiply cheyyali

steps.why: Parity is decided by comparing f(−x) with f(x), so f(−x) must first be written in the same letters as f(x). The negative power e⁻ˣ is what blocks the comparison, and clearing it is the whole of this step.
common_mistakes: Forgetting the minus sign on the middle term and writing −x/2 as x/2.
Treating e⁻ˣ as −eˣ, which is not the same thing.
Cancelling the sign wrongly and writing −x/(e⁻ˣ − 1) as x/(eˣ − 1).

steps.label: Compare with f(x)
steps.margin_note: The second mark is the comparison. Split eˣ as (eˣ − 1) + 1 so the extra x appears, then cancel it against −x/2 to get +x/2.
steps.memory_tip: Write eˣ as (eˣ − 1) + 1. The first piece cancels the denominator and leaves a plain x, and x − x/2 is x/2.

lines.text: ∴ f is an even function on R − {0}.

recall.must_convey: That splitting eˣ as (eˣ − 1) + 1 gives f(−x) = x + x/(eˣ − 1) − x/2 + 1, which is x/(eˣ − 1) + x/2 + 1 = f(x), so f is even.

then x minus x by two is x by two
so f of minus x is exactly f of x and the function is even
x minus x by two equals x by two so f of minus x equals f of x, even function

steps.why: The extra x produced by the split is exactly what the term −x/2 needs: x − x/2 = x/2, which is the middle term of f(x). A numerical check agrees — at x = 0.6 both f(0.6) and f(−0.6) are 2.0298, and at x = 1.7 both are 2.2300.
common_mistakes: Writing x − x/2 as −x/2, which would give a false odd conclusion; the correct value is x/2.
Stopping at f(−x) = xeˣ/(eˣ − 1) − x/2 + 1 and asserting it equals f(x) with no algebra.
Concluding odd because a minus sign appeared during the working.
